//: Sound (Phase 6). Every sound is synthesised at load in a worker (src/audio/voices.ts recipes, src/audio/bank.ts lists them) and played through WebAudio from the broadcast camera (src/audio/engine.ts), driven by the sim's events, the players' feet and a crowd that follows the match (src/audio/soundscape.ts). DECISIONS.md (Phase 6) has the reasoning and sources; tests/audio holds the measurable parts.
//variants: Renders of each sound per parameter bin; play picks one at random (never the one just played) and varies its pitch +-3% and level +-1.5 dB, so no two hits are the same. Three or more of anything heard often: with two, never repeating the last makes a strict A/B/A/B (the applause after every point alternated between two renders).
//peak: dBFS peak of the loudest render of each family, heard at the reference distance. Impacts follow a law below it (bank.ts `law`: a bin's level goes with its speed or force, the bins only change the timbre). Bounces, steps and scuffs are levelled on turf: other floors keep their own loudness against it (a resin court is louder than sand). The racket leads; the glass is nearly as loud (the 'bang' is what neighbours complain of); shoes are a texture under the play; a bird is a call in the trees.
//rms: Crowd and ambience beds by loudness (RMS dBFS of the loudest render), not peak; reactions (applause, ooh, aah, cheer) by the rms of the part that sounds, capped at -9 dBFS peak. These are the stadium's 4,600; a smaller crowd is quieter by 10 log10(N / 4600) (power with headcount), +6 dB for a club's few watchers sitting by the court (bank.ts crowdDb): 8 people clap 22 dB under the stadium. A clean drive is about -30 dBFS over its first 50 ms: the crowd's chatter between points sits 10 dB under it (hushed 16 dB further in a point), a big applause a little over it, as on a broadcast after a great point.
//distance: From the broadcast camera (the listener): ref is the near baseline's distance, where a sound plays at its family level; the inverse law with this rolloff makes the far baseline (36 m) about 6 dB quieter. Air and distance take the highs: lowpass at airHz / (1 + d / airM).
//master: dB before the safety limiter (a compressor at -2 dBFS, hard knee, 20:1, its automatic make-up gain taken back out, so it is unity below -2 dBFS) and a clip that passes everything under 0.8 unchanged and rounds off above: the mix tests (tests/audio/bank.test.ts) hold the busiest moments of every arena and floor under the limiter's threshold.

stadium.//room: A big indoor arena: RT60 about 2 s in the mids (an estimate for a full hall; BB93 caps school sports halls at 1.5 s, arenas run longer), longer in the lows, shorter in the highs (air and seats). Early reflections: the court's own glass (12-24 ms), the roof (19 m up: 66 ms), the end wall (108 ms), the side walls.

hall.//room: A covered club: a steel shed with open or half-open sides. RT60 about 1.25 s (BB93's 1.5 s ceiling for sports halls; the open sides let sound out). The bare roof about 9 m over a hard floor gives a flutter echo every 52 ms.

club-day.//room: Outdoors: no room, only the court's glass (side and far walls, 14-58 ms), a little from the neighbours' cages and the clubhouse (120 ms) and a short tail.

//crowd: The murmur bed's level (dB from its rms) between points (chatter), from the server's set-up through the point (hush: 'silence, please'), and how much it rises over a long rally (tension: back to near chatter level by about 22 shots, the buzz of a crowd on the edge of its seats). Crowds under `big` don't cheer or gasp as one; they clap. The stadium has its air handling under the play (the hall bed).
